hint_retention_days: How long individual pageviews are kept (before being folded into the daily summaries) before being deleted automatically. 0 = keep forever. The aggregated statistics themselves are unaffected and are kept indefinitely regardless of this setting.
hint_geoip_no_data: No GeoIP data has been loaded yet - this setting currently has no effect until an IP-range table is imported.
hint_site_host: Used to exclude internal navigation (e.g. clicking from one page of this site to another) from the referrer breakdown.
label_file_ready: Ready to import (%s MB) - just click "Import", no upload needed.
hint_upload_csv: Expected format: one line per IP range, no header row: start_ip,end_ip,country_code (e.g. 1.0.0.0,1.0.0.255,AU). CIDR notation (1.0.0.0/24,AU) is also accepted. An import fully replaces the previous GeoIP data.
msg_geoip_upload_failed: The file could not be uploaded.
msg_geoip_no_file: Please upload a file or choose an existing one.
msg_geoip_imported: Import complete: %s IP ranges imported, %s rows skipped (invalid).
intro_rawdata: Individual pageviews before they are rolled up into daily totals - including the ones detected as bots. Use this to see what is behind suspicious numbers and to mark a user agent as a bot directly.
msg_raw_db_unavailable: The raw data database (data/tracker-raw.sqlite3) could not be opened. Is the data/ directory writable? See the PHP error log for details.
label_raw_available: Raw data available from %s. Times in UTC.
hint_show_hits: Show individual hits of this user agent
hint_show_agents: Show user agents of this page
hint_mark_bot: Enter a short, distinctive part of the user agent (no regex). Existing raw data is re-evaluated right away.
hint_ua_looks_like_browser: This looks like a regular browser. A pattern here would also catch real visitors - bots like this are usually caught by the header filter.
hint_rawdata_limits: Shows at most 100 groups or the 200 most recent hits. Hits detected as bots are deleted after the configured bot retention period.
label_bots_filtered: %s bot hits filtered out in this period (see Raw data).
label_bot_header_filter: Treat requests without typical browser headers as bots
hint_bot_header_filter: Real browsers always send a language (Accept-Language) and, over HTTPS, the Sec-Fetch headers. Scrapers faking a browser user agent usually omit them. The Sec-Fetch check only applies to HTTPS requests.
hint_raw_hits_caught: Hits detected in the current raw data
hint_bot_retention_days: Hits detected as bots are only stored for inspection under "Raw data" and deleted after this period. 0 = as long as the other raw data.
hint_reclassify: Changes to patterns and switches are applied to the existing raw data automatically and the affected days are recalculated. Use this to trigger it manually for all raw data.
hint_custom_patterns: If the user agent contains one of these texts (case-insensitive), the hit counts as a bot. The number shows how many hits in the current raw data the pattern caught.
msg_no_custom_patterns: No custom patterns yet. The easiest way is to mark a user agent as a bot under "Raw data".
msg_pattern_length: The pattern must be 3 to 100 characters long.
msg_pattern_hits_browsers: This pattern also appears in regular browser user agents and would filter out real visitors.
msg_pattern_covered: Already caught by the pattern "%s" - no additional pattern needed.
hint_ua_outdated_chrome: Outdated Chrome version (%d, currently about %d). Chrome updates itself automatically, so real visitors practically never send a version like this - typical for scrapers with a hardcoded user agent. The exact version number is suggested so only this one user agent is caught.
label_bot_outdated_filter: Treat outdated Chrome versions as bots
hint_bot_outdated_filter: Chrome, Edge and Opera update themselves automatically. A user agent with a Chrome version about three years old practically always comes from a scraper with a hardcoded user agent. The current version is about %d; everything below %d counts as a bot. The threshold moves along automatically. This also affects computers that no longer get updates (Windows 7/8, very old macOS versions) - a negligible share today.
label_outdated_threshold: Chrome below version %d counts as a bot
label_bot_query_values: Treat as bot from this many filter values per request (0 = off)
hint_bot_query_values: Crawlers often walk through every combination of a product filter: each combination is a new URL, and each request comes from a different IP address with a different browser user agent. All values in the query string are counted, a parameter with several comma-separated values counts several times. Tracking parameters (utm_*, gclid, fbclid etc.) don't count. Real visitors rarely set more than two or three filters at once.
